title: Head of Content and Media
text:
ABOUT BUTTER

Hi, we're Butter https://butter.video/ 👋

We're building a creative platform where people and AI agents can create together using more than just generation.

Today, creative tools force you to choose. Traditional software gives you control, but takes time and expertise to master. AI can generate content in seconds, but changing or refining the result often means starting over.

Butter brings the best of both together.

Our approach is built around code. Instead of generating flattened videos or images, AI can build fully editable designs, motion graphics, and videos that you can change yourself, or keep working on with your agent. Every element can be adjusted, reused, or remixed without starting from scratch.

We're a small team of engineers and creatives who care deeply about craft, building the tools we believe should exist.


ROLE SUMMARY

As Butter's first Head of Content & Media, you'll build our media arm from the ground up. Think of it as launching a channel from scratch inside a software company. You'll create bite-sized video content on a weekly cadence, test formats and hooks relentlessly, and build a team of editors, motion designers, and writers to scale it. Working directly with the CEO, you'll turn product launches, partner collabs, and tutorials into content people actually want to watch, not feature announcements.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Domains You'll Own:

 - Content cadence and output (2–3 pieces per week to start)

 - Creative direction and hook testing

 - Freelance production team

 - Creator and influencer collaborations

 - Audience growth and content performance

Overall You'll:

 - Stand up Butter's content engine from zero: formats, workflows, and a publishing calendar

 - Concept, script, and direct short-form video that stands out rather than copying what's already out there

 - Run structured experiments on hooks, formats, and platforms, then double down on what works

 - Recruit, brief, and manage a bench of freelance video editors, motion designers, and copywriters

 - Partner with creators and influencers to extend reach through collaborations

 - Turn new features, tutorials, and partner collabs into entertaining, shareable content

 - Build the systems and feedback loops that keep content shipping consistently

 - [Help design a scalable production model, including a potential offshore team]




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years building content, media, or creator programs, ideally with at least one built from scratch

 - Video-first: you've conceptualized, directed, or produced short-form video, not just written content

 - Experience managing freelancers or production teams on a recurring cadence

 - Deep fluency in modern social media: algorithms, hooks, and what makes content spread today

 - A creative point of view that's a little unconventional, balanced with type-A operational discipline

 - A track record of measurable results: views, followers, engagement, or signups driven by content you built


BONUS POINTS

 - You've built your own following or worked as a creator

 - You've run influencer or creator partnership programs

 - You've produced a recurring show, podcast, or episodic series

 - Background in modern digital media, a creative agency, or as a founding marketer at a startup




WHY BUTTER

💪 Built to Last

The most enduring products (Canva, Figma, Notion) took years to get right. We've taken the same path: stayed lean, grew through a passionate community, and tackled hard technical problems that set us up to build something enduring.

Now we've raised $8M+ from top-tier investors. You'll join as an early leader with real ownership and a direct hand in shaping how Butter scales.

❤️ Customer Love

Butter powers video creation for 40,000+ brands, creators and agencies, including Crocs, Netflix and Pinterest, as well as global artists like Blackpink and Future. We’ve grown purely through word of mouth. People don’t just try Butter. They use it daily and tell people about it. You’ll be joining as we enter our next stage of growth.

💨 A Team That Ships

We care deeply about the customer experience and release weekly. We bring decades of experience building products at Figma, Headspace, Meta and Squarespace. Now we're focused on one thing: redefining what creative software can be.

🙌 World-Class Mentors

We're backed by founders and leaders from OpenAI, Shopify, Notion, Airtable and The Browser Company. They've built the products we admire most, and now they're helping us build ours.


WANT TO APPLY?

 

Butter is a well-funded, ambitious team rethinking what creative tools can be. We’re remote-first and distributed, with optional offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Team Lead, Ground Operations (3rd Shift)
text:
As the Team Lead for Ground Operations (3rd Shift), you will drive operational excellence by leading overnight fleet maintenance, rework, and mission readiness activities. Service efficiency and comprehensive fleet preparedness are key drivers of our success, making this role critical to ensuring that vehicle maintenance, reworks, and fleet readiness activities are optimized overnight during low-demand periods. You will be responsible for the holistic readiness of our vehicle fleet, ensuring maximum fleet uptime and vehicle availability for daytime operations.
In this technical leadership role, you will ensure vehicles are configured, maintained, and prepared for service, while shaping a positive workshop and depot culture. You will lead a team of skilled vehicle technicians and readiness and response associates on the overnight shift. By optimizing workflows and taking ownership of mission-critical readiness targets, you will act as a strategic partner to cross-functional teams, translating high-level operational goals into actionable plans for your 3rd-shift crew.
Shift: Friday - Tuesday, 10pm - 6am
In this role, you will:
Strategic Leadership & Team Culture
Overnight Shift Leadership: Provide direct leadership, coaching, and mentorship to both technical staff and contract personnel during the 3rd shift.
Team Development: Engage in the recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training of workshop personnel. Foster a high-performance culture centered on accountability, safety, and continuous improvement.
Resource Management: Assist in creating and managing employee and contractor schedules, including time-off.
Performance Tracking: Support the tracking of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure individual and team performance, providing consistent feedback to help your team achieve its mission.
Continuous Process Improvement: Identify bottlenecks in overnight workflows and implement lean methodologies to streamline maintenance, repair, and fleet readiness processes, driving ongoing operational efficiency.
Technical Execution & Maintenance
Overnight Maintenance Optimization: Lead vehicle maintenance and rework activities during low-demand periods to maximize daytime vehicle availability and service efficiency.
Technical Escalation: Serve as the primary escalation point for complex technical issues, ensuring all work meets rigorous internal quality standards.
Data-Driven Operations: Support the analysis, documentation, and reporting of fleet data to aid in root cause analysis on component and vehicle-level issues, preventing future downtime.
Safety Stewardship: Enforce all health and safety policies in the workshop. Ensure the facility remains clean, organized, and free of hazardous materials in accordance with company and OSHA guidelines.
Mission Readiness & Logistics
Software Deployment: Ensure the correct software and firmware are deployed to the right vehicles at the right time to support morning operations.
Pre-Mission Checks & Ingest: Direct the ingest of vehicles, conduct rigorous pre-mission checks, and ensure the completion of readiness checklists for the first shift.
Logistical Support: Oversee the logistical movement and storage of vehicles to ensure seamless shift transitions.
Vehicle Operations: Manually drive and maneuver autonomous and auxiliary vehicles when needed to support readiness workflows and yard logistics.
Multi-Site Support: Support team and vehicle fleet operations across multiple sites within the geo, coordinating across different Mission Readiness and Base Operations locations as operations scale.
Qualifications
5+ years of hands-on automotive technician experience combined with 2+ years of people leadership or supervisory experience.
Willingness and ability to lead overnight operations (3rd shift).
Extensive knowledge of automotive maintenance methods, diagnostic methods, parts, and tools, including high proficiency in CAN/LIN architecture, wiring diagrams, and soldering.
Proven ability to quickly learn technical subjects.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; must be honest, responsible, and capable of translating technical details for cross-functional stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to manage time, multitask, and drive priorities effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.
Clean driving record and the ability to travel locally and nationally (less than 20%).
Bonus Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in a technical or business field, or a Technical trade school certificate / Associate Degree in automotive repair.
Strong understanding of electric vehicle architecture and high-voltage systems.
Experience in a fast-paced service environment.
Familiarity with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.

title: Full Stack Software Engineer
text:
About Chalk

Chalk (chalk.ai http://chalk.ai) is the platform for production AI. Trusted by enterprises including Whatnot, Grindr, Mission Lane, Turo, and Apartment List, Chalk brings together context, runtime, and learning for agents and models. Chalk’s Context Engine delivers live context by querying data across warehouses, databases, streams, and APIs, straight from the source. Chalk’s runtime powers agents and models with infrastructure and governed access to LLMs and tools. Together, these capabilities help teams build AI that understands their business, continuously improves, and runs reliably in production. We've recently raised a $50 million Series A, led by Felicis. Learn more at chalk.ai http://chalk.ai.

About Chalk

Chalk is building the data platform that powers the future of machine learning applications. We tear down complexity, latency, and scale barriers that have traditionally constrained ML capabilities. Our platform combines Rust-speed performance with elegant tools that developers love to use. Leading companies depend on Chalk for everything from stopping fraudulent credit card swipes, verifying identities, and maximizing clean energy capture. We've recently raised a $50 million Series A https://www.reuters.com/business/databricks-competitor-chalk-raises-50-million-series-2025-05-28/, led by Felicis.

About the role

We are hiring Software Engineers to join our team. This is an opportunity to join us in-person as an early employee and make a large impact at a high growth start-up. You will tackle challenging engineering problems with a high degree of autonomy and ownership. 

We are looking for software engineers who are comfortable solving business problems across all layers of the software stack. At Chalk, we build reliable data processing systems that can operate performantly at scale with a laser-focus on developer experience.

We need engineers who can build world-class user experiences across CLI and web surfaces, while also understanding and contributing to a codebase that contains ideas from compilers, query planners, and distributed systems.



We're in the office 5 days a week. When unavoidable conflicts come up, we’re flexible. This is not a hybrid role.



What you will do

 - Work directly with Chalk’s co-founders to productionize our first iteration

 - Write TypeScript, Python, Go, and React

 - Expose the functionality of our core platform to data scientist and machine learning end-users in their home environments

 - Iterate rapidly to improve Chalk’s platform in response to customer needs

What we’re looking for

 - 4+ years experience of professional software engineering experience

 - Working knowledge of computer science fundamentals. We’re not looking for experience from drilling leet code – we need folks who are comfortable building and maintaining real systems

 - A record of developing sophisticated user-facing applications that are pleasant to use

 - An eye for high-quality UX

 - Track record of learning new concepts quickly

 - Ability to work autonomously & to make pragmatic tradeoffs with an eye towards business outcomes

 - Strong communication skills

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent

Bonus points

 - Experience implementing data infrastructure

 - Experience working with developer tools

 - Experience with applied machine learning or data analytics

 - Experience with Go

title: Senior Product Engineer
text:
About Blacksmith

 - We started by building infrastructure to run CI workloads really fast. Our first product helps companies run GitHub Actions substantially faster and cheaper by owning and operating our own global fleet of bare-metal machines rather than renting generic cloud VMs.

 - Today, we orchestrate tens of millions of Firecracker VMs each week, running CI for 10,000+ companies and tens of millions in ARR. We’ve grown 20x so far in 2026.

 - We operate thousands of bare-metal machines across multiple regions, regularly schedule 300k+ vCPUs concurrently, and run a petabyte-scale Ceph cluster that we manage ourselves.

 - We’ve raised $125M from Seed to Series C, led by Sequoia, Google Ventures (GV) & Peak XV Partners, and we’re intentionally building a small, but exceptional team.

 - Blacksmith was founded by a team with deep systems and scaling experience, including building search/ads infrastructure at Faire, and operating large distributed systems at Cockroach Labs. Our GTM is led by Jon Boyer, formerly Head of Sales at Zapier.

 - We're now extending the same CI infrastructure into a broader platform: running agent sandboxes at scale and building our own background coding agent on top of it.

What you could work on

 - Build and evolve Codesmith, our background coding agent — designing the workflows, UI, and infrastructure that let engineers delegate coding tasks to AI and ship faster

 - Create tools that help engineers and AI agents debug flaky CI jobs: surfacing patterns in test failures, correlating logs with infrastructure signals, and making root cause analysis fast and intuitive

 - Work closely with design to ship polished, high-performance product surfaces across our analytics and observability platform, where engineers go to understand their CI systems

 - Prototype and iterate rapidly on AI-powered features — from natural language interfaces to automated fix generation — and own the full stack from prompt design to backend service to UI

 - Contribute to the architecture of the agent platform: how we run sandboxed workspaces, and orchestrate agent sessions

You are a good fit if you

 - Have strong CS fundamentals and a deep understanding of React and modern frontend development.

 - Can work closely with design to build polished, high-performance UIs — and aren’t afraid to go deep on browser performance, rendering bottlenecks, or complex component architecture.

 - Have 5+ years of software development experience.

 - Enjoy working in person 5 days a week in NYC.

 - Enjoy working at a very early-stage startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.

Bonus

 - You’ve dabbled in your own side hustles or start-up projects.

 - You’re comfortable creating new processes and iterating on them quickly.

Compensation and benefits

 - Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance.

 - Competitive base + equity.

 - 401K match.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Annual offsite.

 - Early-exercise stock options  

 - 12 weeks fully paid parental leave (US)

text:

title: Payroll Tax Specialist
text:
Hi, Future Homie!

At Homebase, you’ll join a team that’s bold, fast-moving, and obsessed with helping small businesses thrive. We build with empathy, act with urgency, and take big swings that drive real-world impact. Here, every Homie shows up to raise the bar, support one another, and celebrate wins as a team.

We’re not just building an app—we’re building unstoppable teams. So what do you say, are you in?


 📍Your Impact Starts Here

We're building something new at Homebase: a dedicated Payroll Tax function within our Payroll Care Team focused on helping customers navigate payroll tax notices, filing questions, and account issues.

As a Payroll Tax Specialist, you'll help customers when payroll tax gets complicated. You'll investigate incoming tax notices, identify what happened, and resolve most issues independently using established processes and your growing expertise. For complex or higher-risk cases, you'll bring a clear recommendation and partner with senior teammates on the path forward.

You'll work directly with customers and closely with our Payroll Care and Payroll Operations teams. Along the way, you'll deepen your payroll tax expertise, strengthen our documentation, and help us spot recurring issues that can make our processes and product better.

You'll also use AI and automation to research issues faster, create clearer documentation, and make customer communication more effective, then measure the impact and share what works.

This is a role for someone ready to grow from learning the craft to owning it. You don't need to know every agency rule or every tax scenario. You do bring solid payroll tax fundamentals, strong attention to detail, sound judgment about when to escalate, and a drive to get better every day.

These are the key ways you’ll contribute and create impact in this role:

Drive Tax Notice Resolution: Primary Focus

 - Review incoming payroll tax notices, investigate root cause, and determine the right next step using established processes and your own judgment.

 - Cross-reference notices against customer tax profiles, payroll history, and filing records to understand what caused the issue.

 - Resolve standard and moderately complex notice scenarios independently, and escalate novel, higher-risk, or high-dollar cases with a clear summary and recommendation.

 - Communicate clearly with customers about what we're investigating, what information we need, and what they can expect next.

 - Partner with Payroll Operations and other internal teammates to move tax issues to resolution and follow through on every open action.

 - Track open notices, customer communications, next steps, and resolution timelines accurately in our ticketing system.

 - Draft agency correspondence and penalty abatement requests, and maintain the documentation trail for each case.

 - Document what you learn and update templates and guidance so recurring cases are handled faster and more consistently.

 - Flag recurring issues and patterns to senior teammates so the broader team can investigate process or product improvements.

Drive Quarterly and Year-End Readiness

 - Help customers prepare for quarterly filings by explaining key steps, gathering missing information, and resolving common blockers before deadlines.

 - Review accounts for missing agency IDs, tax rates, TPA/POA information, and other common filing requirements.

 - Identify accounts that need additional attention and escalate potential risks to the appropriate teammate.

 - Support customers with quarter-end filing and variance questions.

 - Conduct year-end account reviews and flag missing or inconsistent information, such as owner or shareholder changes, that could affect payroll tax filings.

 - Maintain accurate customer and case documentation throughout quarterly and year-end cycles.

Deepen Your Registration and Compliance Knowledge

 - Build working knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll tax requirements through hands-on experience, training, and research.

 - Research agency requirements using approved, authoritative sources and internal resources.

 - Help customers understand agency-sourced registration requirements, deadlines, and filing processes using established Homebase guidance.

 - Help maintain internal documentation covering filing frequencies, TPA/POA requirements, agency IDs, registration processes, and other jurisdiction-specific requirements.

 - Support compliance calendar maintenance and help make sure required customer information is identified and tracked.

 - Recognize when a customer question falls outside established guidance and escalate rather than providing tax or legal advice.

Help Keep Customer Accounts Healthy

 - Review customer accounts for warning signs, including blocked accounts, missing agency information, outdated tax rates, or unresolved filing issues.

 - Flag potential risks to the appropriate teammate before they become larger customer problems.

 - Partner with the broader Payroll Care Team to help close the loop on open customer issues.

 - Share recurring questions, friction points, and customer feedback so we can continue improving how we support customers.

 - Help newer teammates learn established processes as you build your own depth.

 

🚀 The Foundation for Success - These are the experiences and strengths that will set you up for success in this role:

 - 2 to 3 years of experience in payroll, payroll tax, accounting operations, or a related field, ideally at a payroll provider or payroll SaaS company.

 - Working understanding of payroll and payroll taxes, including withholding, FUTA/SUI, quarterly and annual filings, and W-2/W-2C corrections.

 - Hands-on experience with tax notices, payroll corrections, registrations, or similar operational work.

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to work through structured processes accurately.

 - Curious problem solver: you want to understand why something happened, know how to find reliable inf

title: Software Engineer, Full-Stack ML Infrastructure
text:
COMPANY

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.




THE ROLE

We’re looking for a full-stack engineer with focus on infrastructure to build the tools and systems that help Pramaana’s engineers and researchers develop, test, deploy, and operate their work more effectively.

Your initial focus will be DevOps and MLOps: improving development environments and deployment workflows, making experiments and evaluations reproducible, and helping teams understand the behavior, performance, and cost of AI systems. You’ll build across interfaces, backend services, and infrastructure automation—not just maintain scripts or configure dashboards.

This is an early-stage role with scope across the company. As needs evolve, your work will extend into shared capabilities such as identity and access, LLM gateways, API-key management, training and inference platform maintenance, usage metering, and internal applications. You’ll work directly with the people using these systems, turning recurring friction into reliable, self-serve tools.

We’re looking for someone who treats internal tools as products: useful, understandable, well-maintained, and built around the workflows of the people who depend on them.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Improve how software gets built and deployed. Develop repeatable local environments, automated tests, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment workflows. Help make configuration, secrets, releases, and rollbacks easier to manage safely.

 - Build tools for the AI development lifecycle. Create workflows for running experiments and evaluations, versioning datasets and configurations, tracking results and artifacts, and deploying or integrating model services. Make runs easier to reproduce, compare, and investigate. Help researchers get from a recipe to a running job, and from a failed job to the cause..

 - Create full-stack, self-serve applications. Build interfaces and APIs that let teams launch jobs, manage configurations, inspect results, and troubleshoot failures without relying on repeated manual assistance.

 - Make systems observable and costs understandable. Connect logs, metrics, traces, and usage data so teams can diagnose issues, identify bottlenecks, and understand where time and compute are being spent.

 - Contribute to shared platform services. Help build and integrate identity, access controls, LLM routing, API keys, budgets, and usage metering across Pramaana’s products and internal workflows.

 - Use existing tools thoughtfully. Evaluate and extend open-source or managed solutions where they fit. Build custom software where it solves a real gap, rather than recreating infrastructure unnecessarily.

 - Improve tools through direct feedback. Work alongside engineers and researchers to identify recurring problems, prioritize improvements, and measure whether tools reduce setup time, manual work, and failed runs. Maintain tests, documentation, and operational guidance for what you ship.




YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Minimum 2-3 years of software engineering experience, including hands-on work with backend services, full-stack applications, internal tools, or deployment automation.

 - A solid foundation in building software across the stack. You can develop services and automation in Python or TypeScript, work with APIs and databases, and build usable interfaces with React or a similar framework.

 - Practical cloud and deployment experience. You’ve deployed applications using containers and a cloud platform such as AWS, worked with CI/CD, and used logs or metrics to investigate problems.

 - Some hands-on exposure to AI or ML workflows. This could include integrating model APIs, running evaluations, tracking experiments, or operating model-backed applications through work or substantial projects. You don’t need to be an ML researcher.

 - A product mindset for internal users. You care about clear interfaces, sensible defaults, useful documentation, and reducing the number of steps it takes someone to get their work done.

 - Good engineering judgment and a collaborative approach. You write maintainable code, test important behavior, ask for review, and communicate trade-offs. You can take ownership of a scoped problem while recognizing when to seek help.




ESPECIALLY STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Experience with experiment tracking, evaluation pipelines, workflow orchestration, or model observability using tools such as MLflow, Langfuse, or Temporal.

 - Experience with infrastructure as code, container orchestration, or telemetry tooling, such as Terraform, Kubernetes, or OpenTelemetry.

 - Experience running GPU workloads on Kubernetes: job queueing and preemption multi-node training with NCCL over EFA or InfiniBand, GPU node health and driver management, or serving models with vLLM or SGLang.

 - Experience implementing authentication, role-based access, API-key management, image provenance, LLM gateways, usage and cost tracking or hardening public endpoints.

 - Experience adapting open-source software or building developer tools that other engineers or researchers use regularly.

You don’t need experience with every system listed above. Strong software engineering fundamentals, practical problem-solving, and an interest in DevOps and MLOps matter more than matching every tool.

title: Account Executive, Bridge
text:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Our Scaled Account Management team focuses on driving measurable expansion across a broad portfolio of mid-market and high-growth customers through data-driven strategies, efficient processes, and strong cross-functional partnership.

You will combine consultative selling with volume playbooks, prioritization based on quantitative signals, and hands-on execution to identify and close upsell opportunities across your territory. As Bridge continues to develop within Stripe’s Money Management organization, you will also drive your customers’ adoption of additional features available through Stripe.
Responsibilities
- Own a book of existing accounts and drive revenue growth through additional usage, upsells, cross-sells, and renewals.
- Develop and execute scalable go-to-market strategies that increase revenue per account and accelerate product adoption across your portfolio.

- Coordinate with product, success, risk, and operations teams to solve complex customer needs and ensure a great user experience.
- Translate customer feedback into actionable product and process improvements to better serve scaled customer segments.
Who You Are
-5–8 years of full sales cycle or account management experience focused on existing business accounts; experience managing a large book of accounts or high-velocity portfolio strongly preferred.
- Strong analytical skills with experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes.
- Comfortable understanding technical product requirements and articulating solutions across multiple technology products.
- Demonstrated ability to close upsell opportunities and manage complex pricing or commercial negotiations.
- Excellent operational acumen and proven ability to manage time and prioritize across a high-volume territory.
- Highly motivated, persistent, and effective in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills.
- Willingness and ability to work in-office in New York or San Francisco at least three days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
- Previous experience at a high-growth payments, fintech, crypto, or technology company.
- Experience with CRM tools, Excel, and basic SQL or a demonstrated comfort with data tools and analysis.
- Background in working cross-functionally with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver outcomes for customers.
Why Bridge
Join a team that values clear thinking, quantitative rigor, and customer obsession. At Bridge you’ll own meaningful customer outcomes, operate with autonomy, and have the opportunity to shape how we scale revenue across high-potential accounts.

title: Recruiting Coordinator (6-Month Contract)
text:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Recruiting Coordinator on a 6-month contract, you will keep our interview process running smoothly for candidates, interviewers, and recruiters during a period of rapid hiring. You will own scheduling and logistics from first screen through offer, and work closely with our recruiters and hiring managers to deliver a candidate experience that reflects the quality of our team.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own end-to-end interview scheduling, including phone screens, technical interviews, and onsite loops, across multiple time zones and interviewer calendars

 - Coordinate onsite visits at our San Francisco office, including candidate travel, building access, and day-of logistics

 - Keep candidate records, stages, and interview plans accurate and current in Ashby

title: Customer Care Associate
text:
Join Choco, where we build and own solutions that reshape a broken food system.

The global food supply chain is inefficient by design. Waste is high, margins are thin, and most distributor order processes are done over the phone, tracked across broad spreadsheets, and based on intuition rather than strong data.


At Choco, we’re changing that. We build software used daily by food distributors and their customers to run their business. It automates orders, reduces errors, and helps operations run faster and more reliably. Because it’s embedded in daily operations, our SaaS platform has immediate, real-world impact, on efficiency, margins, and how businesses run day to day.

As Customer Care Associate, you will own customer issue resolution end to end and ensure distributors receive fast, reliable support in their day to day operations. You are accountable for ensuring customer order flow stays running and resolving customer issues as they arise.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Working hours

WHAT YOU GET

title: Risk Analyst
text:
About Fin

Fin is a next-generation payments platform built for high-value, global, and instant transactions. We are a Series A-stage company backed by Sequoia, Circle, and other notable investors. Powered by stablecoins, Fin enables users and businesses to move millions of dollars in seconds - whether to other Fin users, directly into bank accounts, or across crypto rails. By combining the speed of crypto with the reliability and trust of traditional finance, Fin reimagines how money moves worldwide. If banks and payment products were reinvented today, they would look like Fin.


ROLE OVERVIEW

We are hiring our first  Fraud/Risk Analyst to join our Risk & Compliance team . This role will focus on identifying, analyzing, and mitigating risks associated with digital asset transactions – including ACH fraud and compliance with applicable regulations like the Patriot Act and Bank Secrecy Act. This is a critical position, reporting directly to the CEO, and will require a combination of technical, analytical, and regulatory expertise to build a robust fraud detection and risk assessment framework from the ground up.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop and implement a comprehensive risk management strategy tailored to the evolving digital asset landscape.

 - Take action to resolve automatically flagged transactions and individuals

 - File suspicious activity reports as required 

 - Monitor and analyze transaction data to detect potential fraud, suspicious activities, and emerging risk trends.

 - Utilize advanced data analysis techniques and fraud detection tools to identify anomalies and potential security threats.

 - Create and maintain risk assessment models to evaluate the financial and reputational impact of potential fraud incidents.

 - Partner with the engineering team to design and implement fraud detection systems, leveraging machine learning and predictive analytics.

 - Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, including AML, KYC, and digital asset regulations.

 - Draft detailed reports and dashboards on risk findings, fraud incidents, and risk mitigation strategies for senior leadership and stakeholders.

 - Lead cross-functional risk assessments for new product launches, ensuring security and fraud prevention measures are integrated into product design.

 - Stay abreast of emerging risks in the digital asset space, including regulatory changes and new fraud tactics.

 - Develop incident response plans for fraud detection and participate in incident response drills to assess and enhance our risk management framework.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Computer Science, Data Science, or related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in fraud analysis, risk management, or financial crime prevention, ideally within fintech, digital assets, or blockchain environments.

 - Demonstrated experience with fraud detection systems, transaction monitoring tools, and data analysis platforms (SQL, Python, R).

 - Strong knowledge of digital asset platforms, blockchain technology, and stablecoin ecosystems.

 - Experience with regulatory compliance, particularly regarding AML, KYC, and financial crime prevention.

 - Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to decision-making.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex risk findings to non-technical stakeholders.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Certifications such as Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), Certified Risk Manager (CRM), or CAMS.

 - Experience with machine learning models for fraud detection and predictive analytics.

 - Familiarity with incident response protocols and risk mitigation frameworks in financial services.

 - Prior experience in a fast-paced startup or scaling fintech environment.

title: Developer Success Engineer
text:
Location: San Francisco (in person)

AgentMail gives AI agents their own email inboxes. We’re looking for a Developer Success Engineer to own the front line between developers using AgentMail and the team building it.

This isn’t a role where success means closing as many tickets as possible. We want someone who can solve technical problems independently, understand what a developer is actually trying to do, and recognize when the same problem keeps showing up.

Your job is to answer the question, figure out why it had to be asked, and make sure we learn from it.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own technical support for developers building with AgentMail.

 - Debug API requests, webhooks, product issues, and integrations.

 - Reproduce issues and determine whether something is expected behavior, developer error, a documentation gap, or a product bug.

 - Resolve the large majority of issues independently without needing to pull in another engineer.

 - When something is broken, isolate the problem and give engineering a high-quality reproduction - or open a PR and fix it yourself.

 - Notice recurring questions and friction across support conversations and surface those patterns to the team.

 - Identify inconsistencies and confusing behavior across our API, documentation, and developer experience.

 - Jump on calls with developers when async debugging isn’t enough.

 - Write concise, technically precise responses that make developers feel like they’re talking to someone who actually understands their problem.


YOU WILL BE A FIT IF

 - You have 2-6 years of experience in technical support, developer experience, solutions engineering, or engineering, ideally working with a developer-facing or API-first product.

 - You’re comfortable reading API documentation, inspecting requests and responses, working with logs, and reproducing technical issues.

 - You can distinguish between a bug, expected behavior, and incorrect API usage without immediately escalating to engineering.

 - You can write code to investigate issues and ship small fixes.

 - You’re an unusually clear and concise communicator.

 - You’re resourceful. When you don’t know the answer, your instinct is to investigate rather than hand the problem to someone else.

 - You have strong interpersonal instincts and genuinely care about understanding why a customer is frustrated or confused.

 - You notice patterns. Answering the same question for the fifth time makes you want to fix the underlying problem.


WHAT THIS ROLE ISN’T

This isn’t traditional customer success or account management. You won’t spend your day running check-in calls or forwarding technical questions to engineers.

You’ll be expected to understand the product deeply enough to investigate most problems yourself - and to turn what you learn from customers into signal for the people building AgentMail.

title: Senior Product Designer,  User Infrastructure
text:
Weave's Users Infra team builds the foundation every other Weave product depends on — how people sign in, who they are, what they can access, and how multi-location businesses are organized inside our platform. As the designer on this team, you'll care for the surfaces thousands of dental, medical, and veterinary offices meet on their first day with Weave and use every day after: single sign-on, user and permissions management, workspaces, and the settings that hold it all together. You'll work in a close triad with a product manager and an engineering manager who both have deep history in this domain, and you'll report to a Product Design Manager who trusts your judgment and will make room for you to use it.

 - This position is remote (US-based)

 - Reports to: Product Design Manager, Product Design




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Design end-to-end experiences for single sign-on and authentication — setup, identity configuration, MFA, and the error and recovery states that determine whether a customer gets in or calls support.

 - Enterprise-level user management flows: SSO configuration including group mapping and management of custom roles and access patterns.

 - Shape how multi-location organizations are modeled in Weave — workspaces, org hierarchy, and account switching for customers running anywhere from two operatories to a hundred locations.

 - Create platform patterns other Weave product teams can build on, and contribute them back to our Design System.

 - Ground your work in evidence: talk with customers, explore Pendo and Sigma, and use what you learn to guide the team toward or away from a direction.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO ACCOMPLISH THE JOB

 - You have 5+ years designing software products, including meaningful time on B2B or platform surfaces such as admin, settings, identity, or permissions.

 - You can walk us through two or more case studies that trace your thinking from problem framing through end-to-end user flows and interactions — not just final screens or static states.

 - You design complex, multi-step, cross-platform flows and consider edge, error, and empty states as part of the work rather than after it.

 - You explain your design thinking clearly in writing and in conversation with engineers, partners, and leadership.




WHAT WILL MAKE US LOVE YOU

 - You've designed identity, access management, or multi-tenant products, and you enjoy talking about what made them hard.

 - You've contributed components or patterns to a design system other teams relied on, and you know when to deviate from one.

 - You've worked in healthcare, dental, veterinary, or another regulated industry and understand what compliance does to a user flow.

 - You've run user interviews and used product analytics (Pendo, Sigma, Domo, or equivalent) to inform your decisions.

 - Ambiguity is interesting to you. The problem arrives as "SSO is confusing" and you help turn it into a scoped, sequenced plan.

 - You share work before it's finished and would rather be corrected early than praised late.

title: Medical Assistant & Family Advocate (Field)- Charlotte NC
text:
Who is Nest Health?

As the first value-based care provider built for families, Nest is on a mission to make comprehensive medical, behavioral, and social care radically accessible to America’s highest risk families. Founded in 2022 by Former Secretary of Health of Louisiana and practicing OB-GYN, Dr. Rebekah Gee, and Rebecca Kavoussi, Nest is the first-of-its-kind family-based, in-home, and virtual care model; this includes primary adult and pediatric care, mental health and nutrition support, vaccinations and labs, same-and-next-day acute visits, chronic condition and transitions of care management, social services and navigation, and more. Nest’s innovative model has resulted in partnerships, unlocking care for thousands of families across our markets. Nest’s early success has led to national traction across states and payers, laying the groundwork for future expansion to families across the United States.  

 

What does it mean to be a part of a startup?

Working at a healthcare startup can be a unique experience with a fast-paced, ever-changing environment that can involve varied workloads, quick changes, and high expectations. Taking a position at a Healthcare startup allows for the opportunity to be high impact in disrupting the US healthcare system. You will have the chance to be creative, solution oriented, and have your voice heard! You will need to be flexible, accountable, and self-sufficient, and you might take on multiple roles. Here are some things you can expect: 

 - Role Breadth- Your role may be less defined than in other settings, with the need to wear multiple hats & juggle various responsibilities

 - Learning opportunities- you will have the opportunity, at times, to function outside of your standard position and learn about new roles & areas

 - Fast Paced- Startups often must move faster than traditional large companies. This means you may be asked to cope with or advise on quick changes regarding systems or processes

 - Autonomy- You will need to be highly autonomous, as there is less structure and learning and development than at large orgs. This requires you to be able to learn asynchronously, as well as raise your hand when help is needed, or gaps are identified

 - Collaboration- With so many opportunities to build processes and improve how we deliver care to our patients, we rely heavily on one-another to communicate changes effectively to ensure seamless support across functions. This often requires this individual to give and receive feedback frequently and communicate challenges or opportunities effectively. 


WHAT WILL YOU DO?

 - Provide direct patient care and support for a panel of patients in the home setting which may include but not limited to the following:

 - Perform tasks under the direction of the licensed provider including taking vital signs, updating patient history, collecting lab specimens, and assisting with exams

 - Administer oral, topical, and injectable medications and/or vaccinations

 - Interview patients and record medical history including standardized screening questionnaires

 - Assist providers in procedures using aseptic techniques

 - Adhere to infection control standards including, but not limited to, hand hygiene, use of PPE, and isolation of patients with known infectious disease.

 - Complete accurate EMR documentation of patient information and services provided per the requirements of Nest Health

 - Demonstrate effective teamwork, communication, and collaboration as part of an interdisciplinary care team

 - Assists in patient registration, administrative workflows, and prior authorization approvals

 - Fulfill clerical responsibilities which may include, sending/receiving/scanning medical records, obtaining diagnostic reports, hospital notes & referral information, completing forms/requisitions, managing the charting process & sending specimens to labs

 - Actively participate in all compliance-related matters including, but not limited to, equipment, laboratory tests, medications, and vaccine inventory

 - Provide information and assistance through advocacy, navigation support, and education to Nest families on availability and eligibility of health and social care services. Follow up with families to ensure they were able to access the resources provided/suggested by Nest

 - Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team to proactively contact families and ensure they are connected to the providers, resources, support they need to meet their family health goals

 - Participate in outreach efforts to Nest families including explaining program details to potential families




WHAT DO YOU BRING TO THE NEST?

 - Successful completion of an accredited Medical Assistant program

 - Fluency in English is required for this position

 - High School Diploma or equivalent required: 1-3 years of relevant experience

 - US work authorization

 - Vital Signs and phlebotomy experience: 1 year

 - EMR Systems experience: 1 year

 - Active BLS certification

 - Experience in counseling, community work or community health activities in a government agency or community-based organization engaged in providing services to the public, assisting members of the community in obtaining services is a plus

 - Demonstrating strong communication and interpersonal skills; ability to interact with multiple constituencies and exercise “people skills”

 - Demonstrate ability to exercise standards of professionalism, including appearance, presentation, and demeanor

 - Access to reliable transportation and willingness to comply with all the terms of the Nest Motor Vehicle Safety Policy

 - Please note, this position will involve educating and encouraging vaccination against COVID-19


WHAT IS REQUIRED (TRAVEL & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS)?

 - This is an onsite/mobile job that may be providing service in family homes

 - Must have a driver’s license, a car (mileage is reimbursed), auto insurance, and the ability to drive to the homes of Nest familie

title: Senior Regulatory Counsel
text:
ABOUT ALTA

Alta is building global infrastructure for tokenized financial products. On Alta, institutional-grade tokenized bank deposits, money markets, T-bills, equities, and stablecoin payments settle instantly, with compliance executed provably and privately as part of on-chain settlement.

Alta is built to be massively scalable, provably compliant, and cryptographically private. It natively supports agentic payments and connects to a global network of local payment rails. 

Our mission is to build the financial rails the world needs.

 


THE ROLE

This role will advise on strategies for licensing, partnering with companies that are already licensed, and supporting cross-border product offerings. You will be responsible for supporting our licensing, registration and ongoing compliance obligations by helping to design and implement appropriate measures and controls, and by partnering closely with Compliance, Finance, Information Security and other control functions.

You will be a valuable member of the global Legal and Compliance team and will have the opportunity to support a rapidly growing business and the management team to navigate an increasingly complex regulatory landscape. This dynamic role is ideal for someone who enjoys wearing multiple hats and solving complex issues and blockers for our clients, is detail-oriented, willing to take on challenges and changes, obsessively curious and intellectually honest, and thrives on taking actions and delivering impactful results.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Advise the business on providing transaction orchestration services, relying on partnerships with licensed financial service providers to offer Alta’s first products.

 - Advise the Alta business on the licenses needed in key jurisdictions for Alta to deliver financial services directly, and take the lead in developing the company’s regulatory strategy to select the most favorable license types and the sequencing of applications for licenses or registrations.

 - Work closely with the Compliance, Finance and Information Security teams to file and obtain licenses or registrations in keeping with Alta’s regulatory strategy

 - Monitor, report, and influence trends and developments in financial services regulation and the regulation of tokenized assets, actively identifying and anticipating changes that may impact business operations or strategic objectives.

 - Partner closely with Product, Compliance, Finance and Information Security teams to ensure robust compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including regulation of money transmission, stored value/electronic money, securities, derivatives. foreign exchange, and regulation of the use and custody of tokenized assets to deliver these services.

 - Support Product, Strategy, and Management teams on new market entry and new products and features, providing regulatory mapping and licensing advice

 - Select and manage external legal counsel and consultants, ensuring high-quality, cost-effective support to achieve Alta’s regulatory strategy.

 - Support Government Relations outreach to legislators and regulatory agencies in key markets, helping to shape policy and regulatory approaches relevant to the business.


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - U.S.-Qualified lawyer with 8 years of relevant post-qualification experience.

 - Strong regulatory experience gained in the Crypto, FinTech or Banking industry.

 - Deep experience and demonstrated success advising on regulatory strategy and handling regulatory submissions in financial services, ideally including direct engagement with regulators in key markets.

 - Strong understanding of the regulatory environment for tokenized digital assets, particularly as relates to stablecoins, tokenized money market funds, tokenized equities and the use of tokenized assets as collateral.

 - Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally and build trust with Product, Engineering, Finance, Compliance and external counsel.

 - Ability to influence, explain complex legal topics to non-lawyers, and frame business-relevant options and their tradeoffs to enable quick cross-functional decision-making.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience using, deploying or developing AI and RegTech tools to enhance the legal function.

 - Familiarity with Anti Money Laundering, Sanctions, and Counter-Terrorist Financing requirements.

title: Evals Lead
text:
ABOUT ASLAN

Our national security apparatus was designed for an adversary that congregated and operate in the physical world. The threats disrupting our way of life today have gone faceless, borderless, and beyond the reach of any human operator. Aslan builds the autonomous agents that reach them, unmask them, and stop them, before a life can be lost, a household can be bankrupted, innocence can be stolen, or our can be nation subverted.

In 12 months we've gone from founding to live operational tasking and pilots across multiple national security and law enforcement partners. We've proven it works. This role makes it permanent.

We’ve raised $20M to date from Khosla Ventures, XYZ, BoxGroup, 2048, Liquid 2, Precursor Ventures, and others.




ROLE

Aslan builds autonomous agents that run for weeks at a time across many external systems, plan their own next steps, and work toward an objective. Scoring them the usual way doesn't work. Individual outputs look fine. Results come back late or not at all. What we need to know is whether the agent chose well at the moment it chose, and nothing off the shelf measures that.

This is our first quality role. You'll operate the platform daily, build the tooling that catches what you catch by hand, and own the decision to ship. We deploy on-premise on a fixed cadence and can't push fixes after delivery.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Run the platform yourself every day and log what's wrong in enough detail that an engineer can reproduce it.

 - Sample agent plans, get them rated on whether the agent made the right call, and turn the ratings into a versioned dataset. Engineering uses it as a regression suite. The training side uses it as labels.

 - Diagnose whether a bad decision came from the model or from the harness handing it the wrong context, and route each to the right owner.

 - Write and run checks over each agent's full history, and over properties that only hold across the whole set of running agents.

 - Build a simulation harness so a week of agent operation runs overnight against a candidate build.

 - Define what counts as a regression between builds. Measure both whether agents last and whether they get anywhere. A build that only makes them cautious is a failed build.
   
   


WHO YOU ARE

 - You've owned evals for a shipped LLM or agent product, and you can say what your suite caught and what it missed

 - You've built a labeled dataset that got used for training, not just for measurement

 - You've picked a proxy metric because the real signal wasn't available, and you can defend the choice

 - You know when LLM-as-judge works and when it doesn't

 - You'd rather write the check than file the ticket




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Strong Python

 - An evals framework you've run in production: Inspect, Promptfoo, Braintrust, Arize, LangSmith or equivalent

 - Familiarity with agent harness internals: memory, context assembly, tool selection

 - Preference data, process supervision, or reward modeling experience

 - Enough statistics to tell a regression from noise on small samples




BONUS POINTS

 - Evaluating agents that run for days or weeks, where per-episode metrics don't work

 - Systems you can't roll back or reset

 - Graph stores, provenance, lineage tracking

 - Eligible for a US security clearance

text:

This role exists to dramatically increase the speed at which product ideas become real. You will work directly with the Head of Product to take written product specifications, workflow descriptions, existing product patterns, screenshots, and rough Figma-frame descriptions and turn them into polished, coherent, buildable designs.

title: Member of Technical Staff, Generalist - Supercompute
text:
MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF, GENERALIST — SUPERCOMPUTE
SAN FRANCISCO, CA · IN OFFICE, 5 DAYS A WEEK · FULL TIME · 2 OPENINGS


ABOUT D_MODEL

d_model is an interpretability & alignment AI research lab. We partner with frontier labs to turn their models into capable interpretability and alignment researchers, and we use the agents we build for our own independent research. Our team has worked at OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, EleutherAI and MATS, among other places.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The Supercompute team builds the systems our researchers depend on every day: sandboxes for AI agents, AI training infrastructure, tools for monitoring AI agents, and the tools that keep a fast-moving research lab coordinated. We're a small team, where every member owns real projects end-to-end.

We're hiring two software engineers who can take full ownership of at least one internal system; from discovering what researchers actually need, through design and build, to running and maintaining it in production. You won't be handed a spec. You'll sit close to our research team, notice where they're slowed down, and decide what to build about it.

This is a generalist role. You'll move between frontend, backend and infrastructure, and you'll get to learn new parts of the stack as our needs change. If you like breadth, autonomy and building tools that make other people faster, this is the job.


WHAT YOU MIGHT WORK ON

Projects change with what our research needs, but here are the kinds of things you could own:

 - Sandboxes for agents. Design and run isolated environments where our models write and execute code, use tools and run experiments — safely, secure, reliably and at scale.

 - AI training infrastructure. Build and improve our training systems (pretraining, midtraining, & posttraining): job scheduling, cluster management, training cookbooks, experiment tracking and the pipelines that move data and checkpoints around.

 - Research automation. Build pipelines for automating the development of reinforcement learning environments, AI research, and AI self-alignment.

 - Apps that speed up researchers. Build internal tools that help researchers plan, launch, monitor, compare and share experiments, so they spend less time on plumbing and more on research.

 - Coordination and work management. Build the internal systems that help a fast-growing team track work, share results and stay in sync.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own one or more internal systems end to end: design, execution and long-term maintenance.

 - Find researcher problems before anyone files a ticket, and decide what's worth solving.

 - Make sound technical decisions on your own, and explain the trade-offs clearly.

 - Work across the stack, from user-facing interfaces to backend services and compute infrastructure.

 - Keep what you build reliable, observable and easy for others to use.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have shipped and maintained fullstack production software — frontend, backend and infrastructure — and are comfortable picking up whichever layer a problem needs.

 - Have owned a project end to end, from scoping through design, build and ongoing operation.

 - Have strong product sense: you can talk to users, work out what they really need and build something they'll use.

 - Work well with a lot of autonomy. You set direction for your own work, make good technical calls without close oversight, and know when to ask for input.

 - Have experience building internal tools, developer tooling, platforms or infrastructure for other engineers or researchers.

 - Write clearly and communicate trade-offs to technical and non-technical colleagues.

 - Have used AI agents not just as coding assistance, but as components in resilient infrastructure.


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience with machine learning or large language model training, or the infrastructure behind them.

 - Experience with high-performance computing, GPU clusters, job schedulers or container orchestration.

 - Experience building sandboxed or isolated execution environments.

 - Entrepreneurial experience — you've founded something, been an early engineer at a startup, or built a product from zero.


WHAT WE OFFER EMPLOYEES

 - Platinum-tier medical (Blue Shield PPO or Kaiser HMO); dental and vision

 - Flexible PTO

 - Monthly workspace and wellness allowances

 - One conference a year fully covered

 - 401(k) with automatic enrollment

 - $10,000 Lifetime Fertility benefit

 - Catered lunch daily, and breakfast twice a week in the SF office

 - SF Moma museum membership
   


LOGISTICS

 - Location: We currently expect all staff to work from our San Francisco office five days a week.

 - Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. Not every role and candidate combination works out, but when we make an offer, we commit to a real effort, with support from immigration counsel we work with directly.

title: Flight Software Engineer
text:
Be one of the Bedo 100
Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to enable every satellite mission to enter this new orbital domain. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, below 300 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.
As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo’s trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you’re advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.
How We Operate: Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.
Who We're Looking For: Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You’ll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn’t feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.
If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.
What You'll Do
Develop and integrate flight applications in C and C++ for telemetry management, GNC algorithm scheduling, and payload software management, each running as its own process on a publish/subscribe message bus.
Write software for our imaging payload computer: the code that runs the imaging sensor and moves mission data from the sensor toward the ground.
Work directly with our avionics hardware and our Yocto-built embedded Linux, including kernel and device drivers, alongside the engineers who built it.
Benchmark our software to make sure we meet tight timing constraints, and close the gap when we don't (threading, user space vs. kernel space, offloading to hardware).
Verify our software works end-to-end, from ground communication to spacecraft commanding, and take part in integration and test campaigns.
Write and run automated tests using Python at every level, from software-in-the-loop to hardware-in-the-loop, and help maintain the automated CI/CD systems behind them, both software-only and with real hardware.
Your Ideal Skills and Experience:
Strong C and C++ on embedded Linux, including multithreaded applications and how timing and threading actually behave on Linux.
Have set up or worked in a cross-compiled environment: CMake, GDB, and a build system like Yocto, Buildroot, or PetaLinux.
Understand trade-offs when it comes to topics such as memory, processor capacity, hardware offloading, latency/bandwidth, or build versus re-use.
Can use version control such as Git, are comfortable with merge-request code review, and you might be pedantic about how you version your software (like using SemVer).
Demonstrate a core competency in one, or many, of the following: networking communication, distributed computing, publish/subscribe middleware (like DDS), Linux driver development, state machine modeling, real-time operating systems, software/hardware simulations, or pick your flavor of nerding out and tell us!
Most importantly, want to learn, and want to be challenged.
Nice to Have
Hands-on Yocto experience (it's how we build our flight Linux).
Software that has flown, or was built to fly: satellites, launch vehicles, aircraft, or drones.
Software for embedded imaging sensors or camera pipelines (sensor drivers, V4L2, MIPI CSI).
Rust.
Lua, Python or another embedded scripting language.
Spacecraft command and telemetry experience (CCSDS protocols, command/telemetry databases).
Startup experience: comfortable with broad scope, moving fast, and learning along the way.

$116,000 - $135,000 a year

Employee friendly equity compensation
4% direct matching 401k
Health Insurance: 100% employee coverage & 75% dependent coverage
Parental leave and childcare coverage
Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
12 company holidays
$100 monthly wellness benefit
Relocation package if not based in Denver

title: Founding Engineer
text:
Our product helps security teams quickly and accurately detect intrusions in their cloud environment using canaries - decoy tripwires deployed to deceive attackers.


We're at a massive inflection point and this is a hugely exciting time to join the company:

 - We've just raised a $20m Series A https://tracebit.com/blog/series-a led by FirstMark with Accel, MMC, Tapestry and CCL.

 - We doubled ARR last quarter, work with companies like Riot Games, Docker and Snyk, and have grown from 5 people to 26 in 18 months.

 - Our research https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/google-gemini-security-flaw-could-have-let-anyone-access-systems-or-run-code recently helped fix a P1 security flaw in Google's Gemini CLI.
   

We’re looking for an experienced engineer who…

 - Cares deeply about producing high quality work and is ready to dig into the details but is savvy in making the correct tradeoffs on pace vs. quality.

 - Has spent 7+ years shipping software at some degree of scale and/or criticality.

 - At a Product focused company and/or working with at least 1 of the public clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)

 - Is excited by the pace and rate of change that is inevitable in any successful, early stage startup.

 - Gets their energy from getting things done and in the hands of customers but is also here to have fun along the way!

If you don’t fit this bill exactly but think you could make a difference here - please, apply!

Role

Reporting to Niall https://www.linkedin.com/in/niall-gallagher/, our Engineering Lead, and with significant exposure to our CTO and Co-Founder, Sam https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-j-cox/, you’ll join a team of other awesome engineers looking to make their mark on the world.

This includes:

 - Working face to face with both founders, the whole engineering team and our customers and prospects to build a delightful product that solves real problems.

 - Working across the stack, mostly in C# on .NET Core 10 (here's why https://tracebit.com/blog/why-tracebit-is-written-in-c-sharp), but also Terraform and building out our frontend in HTMX.

 - All the good practices you’d expect from technical co-founders who’ve done this before (CD, Infrastructure as code, simple but scalable and powerful architecture)

 - We’re a small, tight team with demanding customers so expect to be shipping every day with very little bureaucracy.

 - We actively encourage AI-assisted development and give every engineer full access to tools like Claude and Codex.

 - We’re based in a Central London office and work here 5 days a week (and everyone we hire will too).


FAQS

How is work organised at Tracebit?

It’s a small, tight team - we have a standup everyday, each team member is usually responsible for delivering something reasonably large for customers and we meet every few weeks to talk about longer term plans. Between that - there’s a tonne of discussions, customer feedback and analysis, but not a huge amount of process, the team is trusted to prioritise where to spend their time.

Where is the office?

The whole team works together in an office right next to Warren Street tube station https://tfl.gov.uk/hub/stop/940gzzluwrr/warren-street-underground-station/ - there are lots of great places to grab lunch nearby.

Are you doing hybrid/remote?

‍Short answer: No, but flexible on a day to day basis.

Long answer: We are set on building the company on a foundation of an office based culture. We are a very early stage company and think that we’ll build the best company at the fastest pace we can whilst also having a lot of fun by physically working together 5 days a week. On a case by case basis (e.g. leaving early for a holiday, staying home for a builder, working remote for a few days to visit family, etc. etc.) we’re very reasonable and flexible. We respect that this is not for everyone.

‍What are the working hours like?

‍We think 9am-6pm will bring a great cadence to work. As a Founding Engineer there will definitely be times you need to pick up work outside of these hours, we’re keen to limit this where we can but also offer flexibility in return.

Can you sponsor visas?

 We can support various types of working visas in the UK, including:

 - Intra-Company Transfer Visa

We are keen to support candidates who require visa sponsorship. Please let us know which specific visa type you might need during the initial application or interview process. Our team is committed to helping talented individuals navigate the necessary visa requirements.

title: Deployment Strategist
text:
Company Overview 

Promise modernizes how government agencies and utilities support people in financial difficulty. We build technology that makes it simple for residents to receive benefits, engage with assistance programs, set up flexible payment plans, and stay on track—while helping agencies increase efficiency, recover revenue, and deliver services with dignity. You'll need to operate comfortably without a lot of structure. We move fast and figure things out as we go. If you need a defined process handed to you before you can execute, this isn't the right seat.

What you'll do

 - Comfort with budgets and numbers. You should be fluent enough in revenue and account economics to make decisions with them, not just report them.

title: Software Engineer (C++ Systems)
text:
THE SHORT VERSION

Thunder Compute runs a GPU cloud on systems software we built from scratch in C++. It lets us get far more out of every GPU than the rest of the market.

You'll write the core C++ behind it, reporting directly to our CTO, Brian Model (ex-Citadel Securities quant dev). The team comes from Citadel Securities, Aquatic, Old Mission, and AWS.

Compensation: $250–325K base, 0.1–0.3% equity, profit-sharing bonus pool (founders excluded). Visa sponsorship and relocation available.


WHAT THE WORK LOOKS LIKE

 - Remove microseconds from latency-critical paths that cross process and machine boundaries.

 - Build high-performance networking and data-transfer paths.

 - Keep low-level runtime code correct under fork, signals, multithreading, and dynamic linking, inside workloads we don't control.

 - Debug production failures that span the OS, the network, and the GPU, with no repro and no playbook.

 - Design allocation, scheduling, failure recovery, and observability across a GPU fleet.

 - Take new systems research from a paper or prototype into production.

It's the hardest parts of systems research and production engineering at the same time. One week you're tracing a synchronization bug across a distributed workload; the next, you're redesigning a hot path.


WHO WE ARE

Series A, with more than $17.5M raised from Matrix Partners, Y Combinator, and angels from CoreWeave, Microsoft, Cognition, and Anthropic. Small team, live in production with real customers, in downtown San Francisco.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - Exceptional modern C++: memory management, concurrency, performance, and systems-level abstraction design

 - Deep understanding of at least one of: operating systems, low-level networking, compilers, distributed systems, or computer architecture

 - Experience building and running performance-critical C++ in production

 - Strong Linux systems programming and debugging, and the ability to reason across unfamiliar layers of the stack

 - Ownership: you push a project from prototype to 100% done under tight deadlines, ship well-tested code without much oversight, and are happy to work directly with customers on hard production failures

Nice to have: CUDA or GPU systems, high-performance networking, distributed computing, compilers, or dynamic linking. Background at a trading firm (Citadel Securities, Jane Street, etc.), a hardware or AI infra company (NVIDIA, SambaNova, etc.), or a systems research group. Competitive programming, open-source, or research that shows strong fundamentals.


LOGISTICS

Full-time, in person five days a week at our office in downtown San Francisco. Relocation support and visa sponsorship available.


BENEFITS

Profit sharing: a bonus pool paid out twice a year that grows with gross profit, plus $3.3M in near-term bonuses unlocked at gross-profit milestones, split by performance.

Daily lunch, dinner when in-office, snacks, and coffee. Offsites and team events. 401(k). Health, dental, and vision insurance.

You’ve built a data agent that understands multiple data sources and provides actionable insights to make decisions.

Who We Are:

Location: U.S. (Hybrid or Remote)
